seen.extent: Three leaves (ff. 179-181): a 12 x 12 square of the numbers 1-144 and a 12 x 12 square of Latin syllables, each with a short Latin instruction.
seen.cipher: A steganographic puzzle of the kind in the appendix of Kircher's Polygraphia nova (1663): a number square that gives the order in which the syllable square is read. The Wuerzburg page captions the leaves as Kircher's enigma for the duke; the key and the message are on the leaves together.

prior_art.edition: Fletcher's edition of Kircher's letters to Duke August (HAB, online), no. 359, 31 Aug 1664: Kircher praises the duke's solution of 'steganographicum meum epistolium' and adds his own solution of the duke's enigmas ('Nomen costae meae Sophia Elisabetha'); Fletcher notes eight further pieces 'illustrating the presentation and solution of the number-substitution code', sent 25 July 1664, at HAB BA no. 359.
prior_art.literature: Vollrath's chronicle of the correspondence: the duke could read the Polygraphia enigma once Kircher explained it (15 June 1664), sent two examples of his own, solved Kircher's ciphered message of 12 July (25 July 1664), and Kircher confirmed the solution on 31 Aug with one correction (Cereris for Celeris). Strasser's studies of the Polygraphia were not opened.

478.key_check: No key to look for: the number square on f. 179v is the key to the syllable square on f. 181r, and the method is printed in Polygraphia nova, appendix p. 23.

478.closed: A solved exchange of teaching puzzles, not an open cipher. Both sides' enigmas of June-August 1664 were solved by their recipients at the time and the solutions are on record: Duke August's solution of Kircher's message (his letter of 25 July 1664, with eight worked pieces at HAB BA no. 359) and Kircher's confirmation and his own solution of the duke's (31 Aug 1664, Fletcher's edition no. 359; Vollrath's page). The leaves carry key square and message square together. The full plaintext was not copied out here.

590.unvetted: Cluster of four archive units with no single identified cipher document, and the printed edition not checked item by item. Archivportal-D records fetched: GStA PK VI. HA Nl Braunschweig-Bevern Nr. 3 (Apr-May 1757) holds cabinet orders of Frederick II to Bevern, Bevern's reports and 'Schriftwechsel mit Generalfeldmarschall Schwerin - meist in Geheimschrift (Ziffernchiffre)'; Nl Schweden, U. v., Nr. 3 is 'Koenig Friedrich II. an die Koenigin Ulrike von Schweden (chiffrierte Briefe)', undated. Neither record says whether the recipients' decipherments are on the leaves, which is usual for received cabinet orders. The king's orders to Bevern and Schwerin of 1756-57 are printed in clear in the Politische Correspondenz vols 13-15 (friedrich.uni-trier.de), so each ciphered order needs matching against its number there before anything is called open; that was not done, and the digitised Lehwald order (Bundesarchiv RH 18/1732) was not opened. The Bevern-Schwerin exchange and the letters to Ulrike are the pieces least covered by print. known.py 'Braunschweig-Bevern', 'Lehwald', 'Ulrike': only this entry's rows.
